comparator.name: Art History
comparator.sourceNotes: The 180 EC full-time programme has a common curriculum in art, architecture and landscape history. This example uses a faculty-wide heritage course and the Art and Architecture excursion. The 30 EC minor remains open choice.
components: Beyond Antiquity: Art and Architecture until 1750
Gardens and Parks: The Green Heritage of Europe
Paint, Plaster, Plant: How To Do Art History
Into the Fields: Ecologies of Art, Architecture and Landscape
Cultural Heritage: Classical Worlds and the Making of Heritage
Art and Architecture of the Netherlands in Global Contexts
Early Art Worlds: Invention and Exchange in Transcultural Comparison
Caring for the Past: History and Theories of Preservation in Art, Architecture and Landscape
Things and Theories: On Concepts, Objects, and Interpretation
From Studio to Exhibition: Practices and Publics in Contemporary Art
Cultural Heritage: Heritage in a Changing World

Architectural history, urbanism and relationships among artworks, cities and landscapes

adjacent: Landscape history, ecology and environmental relationships in visual and material culture
questions: How art, heritage and institutions shape public memory, identity, ethics and social life

candidates.label: Modern Art, Museums and Visual Media

selection.assessment: The broad option studies art history, heritage and visual culture. The other options prioritise modern museums and media, or landscapes and ecology. They differ by 52.5, 97.5 and 97.5 EC each way. Three coherent options reach the maximum.

alternatives.label: Art History, Heritage and Visual Culture
alternatives.labelReason: Art history and archaeology ground advanced work on museums, heritage and art historiography. Building with Nature introduces how people design and adapt landscapes.
alternatives.concept: Study how art and objects record cultural change. Combine art history, archaeology and heritage with museum studies, visual media and research into how objects and places are interpreted.
progression: Art history and archaeology ground advanced work on museums, heritage and art historiography. Building with Nature introduces how people design and adapt landscapes.

alternatives.label: Modern Art, Museums and Visual Media
alternatives.labelReason: Introductory film and art history support modern museum study, documentary, adaptation and analysis of representation.
alternatives.distinctness: Museum study, modern media, histories of gender and public communication carry more weight.
alternatives.concept: Study how modern art, museums and screen media shape public memory. Combine exhibition and art-historical study with documentary, popular media and analysis of representation.
progression: Introductory film and art history support modern museum study, documentary, adaptation and analysis of representation.

alternatives.label: Landscape, Ecology and Cultural Heritage
alternatives.labelReason: Sustainability foundations support geospatial observation and spatial planning. Building with Nature precedes Living with Water. Art history and heritage connect these methods to places and public meanings.
alternatives.distinctness: Spatial planning, ecology, water governance and historical perspectives on land shape this option.
alternatives.concept: Study how people shape, use and interpret landscapes. Combine cultural heritage and environmental media with ecology, water governance and spatial planning.
progression: Sustainability foundations support geospatial observation and spatial planning. Building with Nature precedes Living with Water. Art history and heritage connect these methods to places and public meanings.

blocks: Both study major artistic periods and practise visual analysis. Groningen gives more attention to pre-1750 architecture.
Both examine how collecting, restitution and public choices shape heritage. UCR centres African art.
Both study artistic exchange across cultures. UCR focuses on Renaissance Italy and its connections with other regions.
Both examine classical culture and its continuing public significance. UCR focuses on Athenian democracy and heritage.
Groningen studies architecture from 1750 to the present in a dedicated course.
Groningen examines changes in architectural ideas and practice in a separate course.
Groningen studies Dutch art and architecture in a global context.
Groningen studies the history and theory of preservation across art, buildings and landscapes.
Students take one excursion. This example uses the Art and Architecture option.
Modern art, museums and visual media
Both study modern and contemporary movements and artistic practices. UCR also examines museums and exhibitions.
Groningen follows contemporary art from the studio to exhibition. UCR addresses exhibitions within its modern art and museums course.
Both examine how people design and reshape landscapes. UCR focuses on water management and nature-based infrastructure.
Both study how cultural works respond to environmental questions. UCR focuses on media, while Groningen combines art, architecture and landscape.
Groningen studies the design and cultural history of European gardens and parks.
Groningen applies concepts and theoretical frameworks to the interpretation of objects.
Both compare approaches to interpreting art. Groningen also teaches hands-on analysis of materials, objects and buildings.
Students complete 30 EC through a minor or approved study abroad.
Students investigate current projects in art, architecture and landscape.
Groningen requires an individual thesis. Independent research at UCR is optional.

notes.text: Groningen teaches dedicated sequences in art, architectural and landscape history and requires an excursion and thesis. UCR offers related study in visual art, heritage, museums and environmental approaches to landscapes.

courses: New Issues in Contemporary Social Theory

audience.programmeDescription: Art History at the University of Groningen studies visual art, buildings and landscapes in their historical and environmental contexts. The degree combines interpretation, field study and independent research.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The closest UCR option combines art history and heritage. The other options focus on modern art and media or on landscapes and ecology. Groningen offers dedicated architectural and garden history and requires an excursion and thesis.
